claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my daughter Alex, she's 4 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your daughter, Alex, who is 4 years old.

To help me assess your eligibility, I need to ask some questions about your circumstances. Let me start:

**Are you currently residing in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status? (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or have another immigration status?)**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Birmingham. I'm a British citizen, so no issues with residency or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that. Being a British citizen living in the UK is helpful for your eligibility.

Now I need to ask about your work and National Insurance contributions:

**Are you currently working, and if so, are you paying National Insurance contributions? Also, do you have a National Insurance number?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm working and I do pay National Insurance. I have a National Insurance number, yes - I've been working and paying in for years now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's useful information. Thank you for confirming that.

Now I have a few questions about your household and family circumstances:

**Are you the only person with parental responsibility for Alex, or does another person (such as the other parent) also have parental responsibility for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex's dad also has parental responsibility - we're not together anymore, but he's still her father.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that. That's an important detail.

Now I need to clarify the living arrangements:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does she spend time with her father as well? If she does spend time with both of you, roughly how is the time split between you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She lives with her dad actually. They live together full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's an important detail for assessing eligibility.

I need to ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit, or has Child Benefit previously been claimed for Alex by anyone else (such as her father)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Her father is already claiming Child Benefit for her, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the circumstances you've described:

- Alex lives with her father full-time
- Her father already has parental responsibility and is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Under UK Child Benefit rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time. Since Alex's father is already receiving Child Benefit for her, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Additionally, Child Benefit is paid to the person with whom the child lives. Since Alex lives with her father full-time, he is the appropriate person to receive the benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear you're not eligible in this case. However, if your living arrangements with Alex were to change in the future and she were to live with you full-time, you could potentially claim Child Benefit at that point. If that does happen, you're welcome to get in touch again to reassess your eligibility.

Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
